voci.proprieta: disorder of the solvent in the dioxane solvate (4:1)

voci.proprieta: disorder of the solvent in the mTHF solvate (2:1)
voci.citazione: The mTHF solvate is a 2:1 solvate, with disorder at one of the solvent sites. Two main positions were successfully modelled with occupancies 0.591:0.409, but it is likely that more overlapped positions were present with very low occupancy.

voci.qualitativo: heavily disordered solvent, impossible to model: PLATON SQUEEZE used
voci.citazione: The EA solvate is a channel solvate with a heavily disordered solvent, probably in many positions within the channel. All attempts to explicitly model the solvent molecules failed.

voci.proprieta: twinning of the acetone solvate

voci.citazione: The structure of the acetone solvate was twinned (Cooper et al., 2002 ▸).

voci.proprieta: residual electron density near the chlorine atom

voci.proprieta: electrons found by PLATON SQUEEZE in the voids of the EA solvate

voci.proprieta: XRPD acquisition: radiation, range, generator, step, time step
voci.citazione: X-ray beam Cu Kα (λ = 1.542 Å), 5–40° 2θ measured range, 45 kV excitation voltage, 40 mA anodic current, 0.016° 2θ step size, 0.3 s time step.
voci.note: diffrattometro X'PERT PRO MPD PANalytical

voci.proprieta: XRPD sample geometry: area/thickness ratio
voci.citazione: Measurement was carried out on a flat sample with an area/thickness ratio equal to 10/0.5 mm.

voci.proprieta: XRPD primary beam optics: Soller slits and fixed slit
voci.citazione: The 2.5° Soller slits with a fixed slit width of 0.6 mm and automatic anti-scatter slits were used to correct the primary beam.

voci.proprieta: XRPD irradiated area of the sample
voci.citazione: The irradiated area of the sample was 10 mm.

voci.proprieta: XRPD secondary optics
voci.citazione: The secondary optics consisted of 2.5° Soller slits and 5.0 mm anti-scattering slits to correct the secondary beam.

voci.proprieta: solution 1H NMR repetition delay
voci.citazione: Samples were dissolved in d6-DMSO and 1H NMR spectra were measured by a Bruker Avance Neo 500 NMR spectrometer equipped with a Prodigy probe and a repetition delay of 10 s.

voci.proprieta: solid-state NMR probe and spinning rate
voci.citazione: 13C and 15N CP-MAS solid-state NMR spectra were obtained using a Bruker Avance III 400 WB spectrometer equipped with a 4 mm probe and with 13 kHz spinning.

voci.proprieta: DSC nitrogen flow
voci.citazione: The samples were weighed in an aluminium pan (10 mg). The pan was covered and the measurement was carried out under a nitrogen gas flow of 50 ml min−1.
voci.note: la massa (10 mg) e il crogiolo coperto sono negli eventi E8 e E9

voci.proprieta: DSC temperature range and heating rate
voci.citazione: The range of investigated temperatures was 0 to 300°C with a heating rate of 10°C min−1.
voci.note: la velocita' (10 °C/min) e' negli eventi E8 e E9

voci.proprieta: FTIR range and resolution (Nicolet IS50, ZnSe single-bounce ATR)
voci.citazione: The measurement range was 400–4000 cm−1 and the resolution was 4 cm−1.

voci.proprieta: FTIR spectra normalization
voci.citazione: All spectra shown are normalized and given as percentages, 0% is defined as the smallest value and 100% as the largest value in the dataset.

voci.proprieta: IDR disc preparation: diameter and mass
voci.citazione: The 6 mm-diameter IDR discs were prepared by direct compression of approximately 50 mg of venetoclax.
voci.note: la dissoluzione dei dischi di VEN A e VEN B e' negli eventi E11 e E12

voci.proprieta: IDR disc compression: load and times
voci.citazione: The material was compressed at a constant load of 100 kg, relaxed for 1 min and compressed again at the same pressure for another minute.

voci.proprieta: IDR medium: volume, SDS content
voci.citazione: IDR measurements were performed in 50 ml of phosphate buffer solution (pH 6.8) with the addition of 0.1% sodium dodecyl sulfate at a stirring speed of 100 rpm.
voci.note: pH 6.8 e 100 rpm sono negli eventi E11 e E12

voci.proprieta: IDR detection: UV spectra interval, optical path, wavelength window
voci.citazione: UV spectra were recorded every 30 s using a probe with an optical path length equal to 20 mm2. The absorbance between wavelengths of 300–500 nm was used to evaluate the amount of API released at each time point.
voci.note: il testo scrive «optical path length equal to 20 mm2» (unita' impossibile per una lunghezza): riportato com'e'

voci.proprieta: IDR evaluation: linear fit window and excluded points
voci.citazione: The IDR was obtained from the linear fit of first 10 min of the measurement. The first three points were excluded because they usually represent the dissolution of the free powder captured on the disc surface during the preparation.

voci.proprieta: CSD-Particle / VisualHabit: force field, charges, limiting radius
voci.citazione: The calculations employed the Dreiding II force field with Gasteiger charges and a limiting radius of 30 Å.

voci.proprieta: hydrogen-bond propensity model: CSD release and distance tolerance
voci.citazione: The HBP statistical model was then generated from the CSD (release 2024), using default donor–acceptor definitions and a 0.25 Å tolerance on heavy-atom distances.

voci.proprieta: hydrogen-bond propensity model: area under the ROC curve
voci.citazione: Model performance during training was assessed by receiver–operator characteristic analysis, yielding an area under the curve of 0.8495, indicating good discrimination between observed and non-observed hydrogen-bond patterns.

voci.proprieta: hydrogen-bond propensity analysis: structures included
voci.qualitativo: all solvent molecules deleted and disorder modelled out (major positions only) before the HBP calculation
voci.citazione: Hydrogen-bond propensity calculations (Rohlíček et al., 2016 ▸; Rohlíček & Skořepová, 2020 ▸): all seven venetoclax solvate crystal structures (VEN AN2, VEN MEK, VEN mTHF, VEN EA, VEN IPAC, VEN DIO and VEN AE), together with the previously published acetonitrile solvate (VEN AN1), were prepared for hydrogen-bond propensity (HBP) analysis in Mercury’s CSD-Materials module.

voci.proprieta: synthon energy threshold for the interaction energy with the solvent
voci.citazione: Table 5 ▸ shows the obtained lattice energy as well as the energy of the interaction between venetoclax and solvent molecules (the sum of synthon energies with values above −1 kJ mol−1; for MEK divided by 2, since it is a disolvate).
voci.note: per MEK l'energia e' divisa per 2 (disolvato)

voci.proprieta: VEN AN2: solvent in discrete cavities
voci.qualitativo: acetonitrile bonded with only weak interactions, in discrete cavities
voci.citazione: The molecules of AN are bonded with only weak interactions and occupy discrete cavities in the structure. The solvent takes up 7.8% of the volume of the crystal.

voci.proprieta: VEN AN2 compared with VEN AN1
voci.qualitativo: similar symmetry and cell parameters to VEN AN1, different calculated XRPD pattern, different conformation and packing
voci.citazione: While it is similar to VEN AN1 (Havlůjová et al., 2025 ▸), described previously, in both symmetry and unit-cell parameters, it exhibits a distinct calculated XRPD pattern. Additionally, the conformation of venetoclax and its molecular packing in the polymorphs are different.

voci.proprieta: VEN MEK, VEN mTHF, VEN EA: isomorphous channel solvates
voci.qualitativo: VEN MEK, VEN mTHF and VEN EA isomorphous
voci.citazione: Three of the novel solvates, VEN MEK, VEN mTHF and VEN EA, are isomorphous (similarities in VEN conformation and packing will be discussed further in the text).

voci.proprieta: channels of VEN MEK, VEN mTHF and VEN EA
voci.qualitativo: solvent in channels along b in all three structures
voci.citazione: Solvent molecules occupy channels running along the b direction in all structures. The solvent occupies between 21.5 and 25.3% of the volume of the crystal in these structures.

voci.proprieta: VEN EA: solvent not modelled, same ratio assumed from theoretical volumes
voci.qualitativo: same API:solvent ratio as MEK and mTHF assumed
voci.citazione: For VEN EA, the solvent cannot be modelled explicitly, but we can assume the same ratio based on the theoretical volumes of the molecules.

voci.proprieta: VEN EA: low-stability solvate with high desolvation propensity
voci.qualitativo: low-stability solvate, high desolvation propensity
voci.citazione: These findings confirm that VEN EA is a low-stability solvate with a high desolvation propensity.

voci.proprieta: VEN IPAC: channels along a
voci.qualitativo: channels along a
voci.citazione: In the structure, solvent molecules occupy channels running along the a direction. The solvent takes up 17.1% of the volume of the crystal.

voci.proprieta: VEN DIO: 2D channels
voci.qualitativo: 2D channels along the ab plane
voci.citazione: Solvent molecules occupy 2D channels running along the ab plane. The solvent takes up 35.5% of the volume of the crystal.

voci.proprieta: VEN AE: cavity solvate
voci.qualitativo: cavity solvate
voci.citazione: VEN AE is a cavity solvate and the solvent takes up 8.1%.

voci.proprieta: VEN H2O and VEN AN1: cavity solvates
voci.qualitativo: both previously published structures are cavity solvates
voci.citazione: Both structures are cavity solvates, and the solvent takes up 4.5 and 7.9%, for the hydrate and VEN AN1, respectively.
voci.note: 4.5% idrato (VEN H2O), 7.9% VEN AN1

voci.proprieta: number of channel and cavity solvates among the seven
voci.qualitativo: two cavity solvates (AN2, AE) and five channel solvates, three isomorphous
voci.citazione: Among these, two are cavity solvates while the remaining five are channel solvates, with three being isomorphous.

voci.proprieta: solvent held only by van der Waals contacts in every solvate
voci.qualitativo: solvent never in hydrogen bonds with venetoclax
voci.citazione: this poses no risk to our analysis since, in every solvate, the solvent is held only by van der Waals contacts and never participates in any hydrogen bond.

voci.proprieta: solvent molecules held only by weak interactions (water excepted)
voci.qualitativo: only the water of the hydrate is hydrogen-bonded
voci.citazione: With the exception of water in the hydrate, all solvent molecules are held only by weak interactions.

voci.proprieta: VEN H2O: two molecules in the asymmetric unit
voci.qualitativo: two VEN molecules in the asymmetric unit
voci.citazione: The structure of the hydrate contains two molecules of VEN in the asymmetric unit, therefore, two marks for each type of interaction are present in the table.

voci.proprieta: starting material, crystallinity and SCXRD as primary method
voci.qualitativo: amorphous starting material; crystals visible in all partially evaporated samples
voci.citazione: As the starting material was amorphous and all the partially evaporated samples contained visible crystals, single-crystal X-ray diffraction was our primary characterization method.

voci.proprieta: all samples were solvated
voci.qualitativo: no unsolvated crystals obtained from solution
voci.citazione: However, none of the measured samples contained only venetoclax, instead, we observed respective solvent molecules incorporated into each crystal lattice.

voci.proprieta: intramolecular hydrogen bonds (1) and (3) in all structures; 3-centric extension
voci.qualitativo: bifurcated 3-centric interactions in all structures except the hydrate
voci.citazione: These hydrogen bonds often form more complex, bifurcated 3-centric interactions by also involving an acceptor from a neighbouring molecule, observed in all structures except the hydrate.

voci.proprieta: amine H-N1: intramolecular (1) or 3-centric (2) hydrogen bond
voci.citazione: In the case of the amine H-N1, there are two options. It can either form an intramolecular hydrogen bonding with O11, marked as (1) in Fig. 4 ▸; or O15 can also contribute to this interaction, resulting in a 3-centric hydrogen bond, marked (2) in Fig. 4 ▸.

voci.proprieta: amide H-N3: intramolecular (3) and 3-centric (4), (5) hydrogen bonds
voci.citazione: An intramolecular hydrogen bond with ether O16, (3) in Fig. 4 ▸, forms in all structures; however, it is often combined with bonding either to tetrahydropyran O10 or to sulphoxyle O13, resulting in 3-centric hydrogen bonds (4) and (5) in Fig. 4 ▸.

voci.proprieta: frequency of the 7-azaindole homosynthon (6)
voci.qualitativo: homosynthon (6) present in 70% of cases
voci.citazione: The N4⋯H—N5 intermolecular homosynthon of 7-azaindole, (6) in Fig. 4 ▸, is also notable, as it is present in 70% of cases.

voci.proprieta: most common hydrogen bonds: (2), (5), (6)
voci.qualitativo: (2), (5) and (6) are the most common interactions
voci.citazione: The most commonly occurring molecular interactions, numbers (2), (5) and (6), will be analysed in more detail.

voci.proprieta: strongest hydrogen-bond interaction and strongest VEN–VEN interactions in VEN AN2
voci.qualitativo: (6) has the highest hydrogen-bond energy; dimers (2) and (5) are the two strongest VEN–VEN interactions
voci.citazione: The N4⋯H—N5 7-azaindole homosynthon, marked (6) in Table 3 ▸, is the strongest hydrogen-bond interaction present in the structure (highest hydrogen-bond energy component). However, the dimers based on the 3-centric hydrogen bonds marked (2) and (5) in Table 3 ▸ represent the two strongest VEN–VEN interactions in the whole structure.

voci.proprieta: aromatic interactions in the strongest VEN–VEN dimers of VEN AN2
voci.qualitativo: parallel offset π–π stacking of nitrobenzenes; herringbone offset π–π stacking between 7-azaindole and nitrobenzene
voci.citazione: The aromatic interactions contributing to this arrangement include parallel offset π–π stacking of nitrobenzenes in one instance and aromatic interactions between 7-azaindole and nitrobenzene in another instance, characterized by herringbone offset π–π stacking.

voci.proprieta: hydrogen-bond propensity of (1) H—N1⋯O11
voci.citazione: H—N1⋯O11 [(1)] carries the highest propensity, 0.93, reflecting its ubiquity and strong geometric preference for forming a five-membered ring.

voci.proprieta: hydrogen-bond propensity of (3) H—N3⋯O16
voci.citazione: H—N3⋯O16 [(3)] likewise scores very high, 0.88, consistent with its universal presence in all ten structures.

voci.proprieta: hydrogen-bond propensity of (2) O11⋯H—N1⋯O15
voci.citazione: The amine bifurcation O11⋯H—N1⋯O15 [(2)] is very unlikely (0.24), in line with CSD statistics that disfavour secondary acceptor involvement in this synthon.

voci.proprieta: hydrogen-bond propensity of (4) O16⋯H—N3⋯O10 and (5) O16⋯H—N3⋯O13
voci.citazione: The 3-centred amide options are both low to moderate: O16⋯H—N3⋯O10 [(4)] 0.13, O16⋯H—N3⋯O13 [(5)] 0.35, indicating only a minority of known structures employ these extended motifs.

voci.proprieta: hydrogen-bond propensity of (6) 7-aza homosynthon N4⋯H—N5
voci.citazione: The 7-aza homosynthon N4⋯H—N5 [(6)] scores 0.52, marking it as a reasonably common and favourable intermolecular network.

voci.proprieta: hydrogen-bond propensity of (7) O13⋯H—N5
voci.citazione: The alternative synthon O13⋯H—N5 [(7)] is even more probable (0.68), yet curiously observed only in VEN AE.
voci.note: osservato solo in VEN AE

voci.proprieta: best predicted hydrogen-bond network: mean HBP and mean HBC
voci.citazione: The highest-scoring network (HBP = 0.518, HBC = 0.878) involves a single intermolecular N4⋯H—N5 homosynthon (6).

voci.proprieta: HBP landscape: hydrogen-bond pairs of the experimental solvates
voci.qualitativo: six solvates with three intermolecular hydrogen-bond pairs, two of them 3-centred; VEN IPAC with two pairs, one 3-centred
voci.citazione: Among the seven experimental solvates, six (green shapes) each present three intermolecular hydrogen-bond pairs, two of which are 3-centred bifurcated interactions and, accordingly, plot at more moderate HBP/HBC values.

voci.proprieta: six of the seven solvates use low-propensity bifurcated hydrogen-bond motifs
voci.qualitativo: six of the seven solvates use low-propensity bifurcated H-bond motifs, probably because the conformational distortion needed also enhances aromatic π–π stacking
voci.citazione: Interestingly, six of the seven solvates employ low-propensity bifurcated hydrogen-bond motifs – despite their unfavourable CSD scores – most likely because the slight conformational distortion needed to form them also enhances aromatic π–π stacking.

voci.proprieta: number of hydrogen-bonding patterns found
voci.citazione: Seven types of hydrogen-bonding patterns were identified among the solvate structures.

voci.proprieta: XRPD patterns calculated from the structures: isomorphous group similar
voci.qualitativo: calculated patterns of MEK, EA and mTHF very similar; the others differ significantly
voci.citazione: The patterns observed for the isomorphous group containing VEN MEK, VEN EA and VEN mTHF are very similar to each other while the rest differ significantly.

voci.proprieta: conformational flexibility: overlay of all structures
voci.qualitativo: intramolecular hydrogen bonds anchor some torsion angles
voci.citazione: The intramolecular hydrogen bonds discussed above affect the molecular conformation of venetoclax, basically anchoring some of the torsion angles.

voci.proprieta: most different conformations (PSab similarity score): hydrate and VEN EA
voci.qualitativo: least-similar conformations: VEN hydrate and VEN EA
voci.citazione: It is an overlay of two least-similar conformations based on the PSab similarity score (based on RMSD), in VEN hydrate and VEN EA.

voci.proprieta: molecular packing: VEN EA, VEN MEK, VEN mTHF isostructural; AN1 and AE similar to a lesser degree
voci.qualitativo: MEK, mTHF, EA isostructural; AN1 and AE similar to a lesser degree; the others distinct
voci.citazione: As can be seen in Fig. S1, VEN EA, VEN MEK and VEN mTHF are isostructural with respect to the venetoclax scaffold, and VEN AN1 and VEN AE are similar, but to a lesser degree (Figs. S4–S5). All of the other structures of venetoclax have a distinct packing of the VEN molecules.

voci.proprieta: interplanar distance shrinkage of VEN AE; small difference of the other two cases
voci.citazione: VEN AE, which partially desolvates upon drying, but does not transform, experiences the largest shrinkage of 5% in the (001) direction. The other two cases exhibit a very small difference, meaning that the VEN molecules probably rearrange/change conformation in such a way that it does not significantly affect the interplanar spacing in the (001) direction.

voci.proprieta: desolvated forms keep the molecular arrangement of the parent solvates
voci.qualitativo: some structural changes on desolvation; overall arrangement likely similar to the parent solvates
voci.citazione: Comparison of XRPD patterns shows some structural changes upon desolvation, but the overall molecular arrangement likely remains similar to the parent solvates, as indicated by the visual similarity of the diffractograms.

voci.proprieta: crystal structure of VEN A and VEN B not solvable from powder data
voci.qualitativo: crystallinity too imperfect for structure solution from powder data; probably triclinic
voci.citazione: Unfortunately, their crystallinity is too imperfect for a structure solution from powder data. Most of the described structures of venetoclax have triclinic symmetry, so there is a strong possibility that VEN A and B do too.

The interaction energies for MEK and AN are comparable.

voci.citazione: The view of the surface molecules provides further evidence of the stability of this solvate, as we can see that each solvent molecule is enclosed within a venetoclax cage, creating a stable, well ordered surface with relatively low rugosity (1.632) and a high attachment energy (−73.936 kJ mol−1).

voci.qualitativo: significant aromatic interactions on (001)

voci.proprieta: VEN AE: stability attributed to strong interactions on the largest face (100)
voci.qualitativo: stability attributed to strong intermolecular interactions on (100)
voci.citazione: This solvate remained stable without desolvation upon drying and this stability can be attributed to the strong intermolecular interactions within the crystal lattice, particularly on the largest crystal face (100).

voci.proprieta: FTIR region of vibrations of hydrogen bonded to other atoms
voci.citazione: Fig. 12 ▸(d) highlights regions which are mostly related to the bond of hydrogen and other atoms, i.e.ca 3500–3000 cm−1, as hydrogen-bond interactions are connected with the hydrogen atom bond vibration frequency change.

voci.proprieta: FTIR: N3-H stretching band (signal 5) in VEN B and VEN AN2; region of the interaction with O13 and O16
voci.qualitativo: strong signal (5) = ν(N3–H) in VEN B and VEN AN2
voci.citazione: In VEN B and VEN AN2, we see a strong signal (5) corresponding to the N—H stretching vibration of N3—H. This band position is strongly influenced by the interaction with O13 and O16, which might be confirmed by vibration band positions and shifts in the region around 1350 cm−1.

voci.qualitativo: no hydrogen-bond interactions of O13

voci.proprieta: 13C ssNMR: crystallinity of VEN A and VEN MEK
voci.qualitativo: VEN A and VEN MEK: weaker spectra, much broader peaks (poor crystallinity)
voci.citazione: In 13C ssNMR, it is very evident that VEN A and VEN MEK have poor crystallinity compared with the other forms (the spectra are weaker and have much broader peaks).

voci.proprieta: 13C ssNMR: carbons adjacent to O10 in the tetrahydropyran ring
voci.qualitativo: two close/overlapping peaks in the solid state (equivalent in solution)
voci.citazione: We have focused on the two carbon atoms adjacent to O10 in the tetrahydropyran ring. In solution NMR, these would be equivalent, but due to the anisotropy of the solid state, they appear here as two close/overlapping peaks.

voci.proprieta: 13C ssNMR: chemical shift when O10 accepts hydrogen bond (4)
voci.qualitativo: peaks of the carbons next to O10 shifted to higher ppm if hydrogen bond (4) is present (VEN MEK, VEN AE; not VEN AN2)
voci.citazione: If hydrogen bond (4) is present, the peaks are shifted to higher p.p.m.

voci.proprieta: 15N ssNMR: N3 and N5 hydrogen-bond donors
voci.qualitativo: same grouping of spectra as for 13C
voci.citazione: The same trends, but on different hydrogen bonds, can be observed in 15N ssNMR. Here, we focused on two nitrogen atoms, N3 and N5, both of which are hydrogen-bond donors.

voci.proprieta: 15N ssNMR: N5-H donor in (6) in VEN MEK and VEN AN2, in (7) in VEN AE; lower shift for VEN AE
voci.qualitativo: only VEN AE has a lower N5 chemical shift
voci.citazione: N5-H is a donor in hydrogen bond (6) in VEN MEK and VEN AN2, and in hydrogen bond (7) in VEN AE. This is consistent with the chemical shifts, with only VEN AE having a lower one.

voci.proprieta: spectral similarity of the desolvated forms with the parent solvates
voci.qualitativo: VEN A ~ VEN MEK; VEN B ~ VEN AN2; the pairs differ from each other and from VEN AE
voci.citazione: VEN A spectra are similar to VEN MEK spectra and VEN B spectra are similar to VEN AN2 spectra. The pairs are distinctly different from each other and also from the VEN AE solvate.

voci.proprieta: VEN AE: interpretation of the hydrogen-bond and aromatic counts of the largest face
voci.qualitativo: balanced hydrogen-bonding network; moderate aromatic bond count, stable π–π stacking
voci.citazione: The hydrogen-bond acceptor count (0.033) and donor count (0.009) suggest a balanced hydrogen-bonding network, with a moderate aromatic bond count (0.056) reflecting stable π–π stacking interactions.

voci.qualitativo: moderate attachment energy, highest rugosity among the three solvates: complex surface topology
voci.citazione: The surface properties from Table 6 ▸ indicate a moderate attachment energy (−66.08 kJ mol−1) and the highest rugosity (2.36) among the three solvates, reflecting a complex surface topology.

voci.proprieta: VEN AN2: hydrogen-bond and aromatic counts higher than VEN AE and VEN MEK
voci.qualitativo: highly interactive hydrogen-bonding network; strong π–π stacking
voci.citazione: The hydrogen-bond acceptor count (0.054) and donor count (0.013) suggest a highly interactive hydrogen-bonding network. The higher aromatic bond count (0.094) indicates strong π–π stacking interactions, enhancing the stability of the acetonitrile solvates’ surface.
